name: VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA)
evidence_rating: ex-ante only: Commission IA and contracted study forecasts; key measures apply 2027-2035 so no outcome evidence yet
summary: The Commission forecast that ViDA would raise EUR 135-177 billion in extra VAT and save businesses about EUR 51 billion over ten years, mainly through EU-wide e-invoicing and digital reporting. These are forecasts for the option assessed in 2022; the main reporting rules only start in 2030, so nothing can be measured yet. The starting point is a VAT compliance gap of EUR 128 billion in 2023.

indicators.objective: The ViDA proposal (a Council directive) has no LFS indicators section; the memorandum refers to the monitoring indicators in Section 4 of the impact assessment and an evaluation 5 years after entry into force

indicators.target_or_baseline: EUR 135-177bn over 10 years (about 0.1% of GDP a year)
indicators.evidence: Not measurable yet: EU-level digital reporting and e-invoicing for intra-EU trade only applies from 1 July 2030 and the package phases in to 2035. Baseline: the EU VAT compliance gap was EUR 128bn in 2023 (Commission VAT Gap report 2025).

indicators.target_or_baseline: EUR 50.6bn savings (41.4bn reporting, 0.5bn platform economy, 8.7bn registration) against EUR 11.3bn new DRR costs
indicators.evidence: Not measured. Commission still cites 'EUR 51 billion in savings for businesses' in its Sept 2025 implementation strategy.
Not measured; single VAT registration measures apply from 2027-2028.
Forecast only; the adopted text differs from the assessed option (some measures softened or delayed), so the figure is an upper reference rather than a forecast for the final law.

literature.citation: European Commission (2022), Impact assessment on VAT in the digital age (executive summary SWD(2022) 394), SWD(2022) 393
literature.title: Impact assessment on VAT in the digital age (executive summary SWD(2022) 394)
literature.outcomes: VAT revenue; compliance costs; administrative burden
literature.headline: Enhanced option: EUR 172-214bn net impact 2023-2032; EUR 135-177bn extra VAT revenue; EUR 50.6bn business savings vs EUR 11.3bn new reporting costs; EUR 2.2bn implementation costs for tax administrations; 280,000 SMEs save up to EUR 7bn
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected the package to bring in EUR 135-177 billion of extra VAT and save businesses about EUR 51 billion over ten years, with new digital reporting costing firms about EUR 11 billion.

literature.citation: Economisti Associati, Oxford Research, CASE, Wavestone et al. (2022), VAT in the digital age: final report (Vol. 1 Digital Reporting Requirements), Study for DG TAXUD, Publications Office of the EU
literature.authors: Economisti Associati, Oxford Research, CASE, Wavestone et al.
literature.title: VAT in the digital age: final report (Vol. 1 Digital Reporting Requirements)
literature.venue: Study for DG TAXUD, Publications Office of the EU
literature.method: ex-ante / comparative review of national DRRs
literature.headline: 12 Member States had digital reporting requirements by Sept 2021; these showed positive net impacts as extra VAT revenue exceeded set-up and compliance costs; fragmentation of national systems identified as core problem
literature.summary_plain: The study behind the impact assessment found that national digital VAT reporting schemes raised more revenue than they cost, but that their patchwork burdens cross-border firms.

literature.citation: European Commission (DG TAXUD) (2025), VAT Gap in the EU - 2025 report, Commission report and data hub
literature.title: VAT Gap in the EU - 2025 report
literature.headline: VAT compliance gap EUR 128bn in 2023 (+1.6 pp on 2022); actionable policy gap EUR 742bn
literature.summary_plain: Before ViDA takes effect, about EUR 128 billion of VAT due in 2023 went uncollected; this is the baseline ViDA aims to cut.

literature.citation: European Commission (DG TAXUD) (2025), VAT in the Digital Age: implementation strategy to support businesses and Member States, News item, 24 September 2025
literature.title: VAT in the Digital Age: implementation strategy to support businesses and Member States
literature.headline: Restates expected benefits of EUR 172-214bn over a decade including EUR 51bn savings for businesses; sets roadmap of action points to 2035
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's implementation plan restates the impact-assessment forecasts and sets out steps to 2035; no results yet.
